title: Use of the MicroSiM (µSiM) Barrier Tissue Platform for Modeling the Blood-Brain Barrier
protocol: Place the membrane chip onto the center of fixture A1 using chip tweezers, flat surface down and trench area up for trench-down devices.
Peel off the blue protective layers on both sides of component 1 using straight tweezers.
Place component 1 in fixture A1 with top chamber down.
Gently press component 1 down until the pressure-sensitive adhesive (PSA) touches the chip.
Put fixture A2 onto fixture A1 and apply firm pressure at different corners to ensure a tight fit.
Bond component 2 to component 1 with the chip.
Prepare component 2 by peeling it off from the sheet using straight tweezers.
Grab the non-PSA "triangle" region of component 2 and remove both the thick, transparent protective layer and blue layer.
Expose the PSA surface after removing layers.
Place component 2 in fixture B1 with PSA side up.
Place component 1 with the membrane chip in fixture B1 with top chamber facing up.
Put fixture B2 onto component 1 and apply firm pressure at different corners of fixture B2.
Take the assembled device out of the fixture and use straight tweezers to press out any air bubbles on the underside.
Seal the edges of the channel, avoiding contact with the membrane region.
Ultraviolet (UV)-sterilize newly assembled devices for 20 min prior to cell culture.
Place the devices in sterile hose clamps.
Soak the clamps in ethanol for ≥20 min to sterilize them.
Rest sterilize the clamps after each experiment for reuse.
Culture the devices in a large sterile Petri dish.
Add a small Petri dish or 50 mL conical tube lid filled with sterile water for extra humidity.
Wash the top chamber of the devices twice with 100 µL of sterile water.
Wash the bottom chamber of the devices with 20 µL of sterile water.
Prepare the cell culture chamber according to section 2.1.
Coat the top chambers with 25 µg/cm² of collagen I and 5 µg/cm² of human fibronectin mixed in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Let the coated top chambers sit for 1-2 h at 37 °C or overnight at 4 °C.
Remove the coating solution from the top chambers.
Add 100 µL of prewarmed growth-factor-depleted endothelial medium to the top chamber and 20 µL to the lower chamber.

Mix 100 mL of endothelial basal medium with 400 µL of human fibroblastic growth factor, 40 µL of hydrocortisone, 100 µL of gentamicin sulfate, and 2 mL of fetal bovine serum to prepare the assay medium.
Trypsinize hCMEC/D3 cells in a 37°C incubator for 3-5 min.
Stop trypsinization by adding prewarmed endothelial medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to a centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the cell pellet in assay media.
Seed hCMEC/D3 cells in top chambers at a density of 40,000-60,000 cells/cm².
Incubate devices at 37°C with 5% carbon dioxide for 2-4 hours to facilitate cell adhesion.
Exchange the medium in both chambers after 2-4 hours to remove dead or unattached cells.
Maintain the devices at 37°C with 5% CO₂, exchanging assay media every 2-3 days until experimentation.
Reconstitute collagen IV from human placenta by adding 5 mL of 0.5 mg/mL acetic acid to 5 mg of collagen IV to create a 1 mg/mL solution.
Let the collagen IV solution sit for ≥4 h at 4 °C to fully reconstitute.
Coat the top chambers with 100 µL of a 4:1:5 ratio of collagen IV, bovine fibronectin, and sterile water.
Coat the top chambers at 37 °C for 2-4 h.
Remove the coating solution from the top chambers.
Add 100 µL of room temperature hECSR to the top chamber and 20 µL to the lower chamber.
Passage EECM-BMEC-like cells according to Nishihara et al.37 by adding a cell detachment enzyme mixture to the cells.
Transfer the detached cells to a 37 °C incubator for 5-8 min.
Pipette the cell solution to singularize and add it to four times the volume of endothelial medium in a centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the cells in hECSR.
Seed the cells in the top chambers at a density of 40,000 cells/cm² by adding 100 µL of a cell solution at 150,000 cells/mL.
Incubate the devices at 37 °C with 5% CO₂ for 2-4 h to facilitate cell adhesion.
Exchange with fresh hECSR in both chambers after 2-4 h to remove dead or unattached cells.
Maintain the devices at 37 °C with 5% CO₂, exchanging hECSR in both chambers every 1-2 days until experimentation.
Coat membrane chips with 2 μg/cm² of poly-L-lysine (PLL) mixed in PBS.
Apply PLL droplets only to the side that will face down in the final device assembly, using 50-80 μL per chip.
Complete the coating process at 37°C for 1-2 hours or overnight at 4°C.
Remove the coating solution from the membrane chips.
Wash the membrane chips with sterile ultrapure water and allow them to dry completely.
Assemble devices with the PLL-coated side facing down according to section 1 of the protocol.
Prepare the cell culture chamber as detailed in section 2.1.
Coat the top chambers according to section 2.2.2.
Add 50 μL of prewarmed pericyte medium to the top chambers.
Add 20 μL of prewarmed pericyte medium to the lower channels.
Trypsinize HBVPs in a 37 °C incubator for 3-5 min.
Stop trypsinization by adding prewarmed pericyte medium.
Transfer the cell suspension to a centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the cell pellet in pericyte medium.
Seed cells in the bottom chambers at a density of 14,000-25,000 cells/cm².
Invert the devices to maintain an air interface with the top chambers.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C with 5% CO₂ for 2-4 h in the inverted position.
Flip the devices upright after 2-4 h.
Exchange both chambers with fresh pericyte medium to remove dead or unattached cells.
Seed hCMEC/D3s in the top chamber after pericyte seeding.
Switch both chambers to assay medium.
Maintain devices at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Exchange assay medium in both chambers every 1-2 days until experimentation.
Exchange pericyte medium with assay medium 2-3 days after seeding HBVPs if comparing with hCMEC/D3 monocultures or co-cultures.
Prepare the cell culture chamber according to section 2.1.
Coat the top chambers according to steps 2.3.2-2.3.3.
Remove the coating solution.
Add 50 μL of room temperature Essential 6 Medium + 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (E6 + 10% FBS) to the top chamber.
Add a cell detachment enzyme mixture to the cells and transfer to a 37 °C incubator for 5-15 min, until ~90% of the cells are rounded.
Pipette the cell solution to singularize the cells.
Mix the cell solution with 4 times its volume of DMEM/F12 in a 50 mL centrifuge tube using a 40 μm cell strainer.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the cell pellet in E6 + 10% FBS.
Seed cells in the bottom chambers at a density of 14,000-25,000 cells/cm².
Invert the devices but maintain an air interface with the top chamber to facilitate gas exchange.
Incubate the cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 2-4 h in the inverted position to facilitate cell adhesion.
Flip the devices upright and exchange with fresh E6 + 10% FBS in both chambers to remove dead or unattached cells.
Seed EECM-BMEC-like cells in the top chamber following steps 2.3.5-2.3.6 one day after pericyte seeding.
Switch both chambers to hECSR.
Maintain the devices at 37°C with 5% CO2, exchanging the assay medium in both chambers every 1-2 days until experimentation.
Place primary antibodies on ice to thaw.
Prepare a 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) solution at room temperature or chill 100% methanol at -20°C.
Create an appropriate blocking solution according to Table 2.
Store the blocking solution on ice.
Vortex the solution if necessary to fully dissolve Triton X-100.
Pipette 20 µL of fixative into the bottom chamber and 50 µL into the top chamber.
Incubate devices for 10 min at room temperature with PFA or 2 min with methanol.
Wash the devices for 3 x 5 min by pipetting 20 µL of PBS through the bottom chamber and 100 µL into the top chamber.
Block the devices for 30 min at room temperature by adding 20 µL of blocking solution to the bottom chamber and 50 µL to the top chamber.
Check for bubbles in the bottom chamber.
Prepare the primary antibody solution by diluting the antibodies in the blocking solution according to Table 2.
Store the primary antibody solution on ice.
Stain with primary antibodies by adding 20 µL of the primary antibody solution to the bottom chamber and replacing the volume of the top chamber with 50 µL of the primary antibody solution.
Check for bubbles in the bottom chamber after staining.
Incubate the stained devices for 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the incubated devices for 3 x 5 min by pipetting 20 µL of PBS through the bottom chamber and 100 µL into the top chamber.
Prepare the secondary antibody solution by diluting the antibodies in the blocking solution according to Table 2.
Store the secondary antibody solution on ice protected from light.
Stain with secondary antibodies by adding 20 µL of secondary antibody solution to the bottom chamber.
Replace the volume of the top chamber with 50 µL of the secondary antibody solution.
Check for bubbles in the bottom chamber.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature protected from light.
Wash for 3 x 5 min by pipetting 20 µL of PBS through the bottom chamber and replacing the volume of the top chamber with 100 µL of PBS.
Make a nuclear stain solution.
Dilute Hoechst 1:10,000 in PBS.
Add 20 µL of the nuclear stain solution to the bottom chamber.
Replace the volume of the top chamber with 50 µL of the nuclear stain solution.
Check for bubbles in the bottom chamber.
Incubate for 3 min at room temperature protected from light.
Remove the stain by adding 20 µL of PBS to the bottom chamber and replacing the volume of the top chamber with 100 µL of PBS.
Image the devices immediately or store them at 4 °C with the petri dish wrapped in parafilm and protected from light until ready for imaging.
Turn on the microscope.
Open the imaging software.
Set the channels according to the properties of the secondary antibody and the nuclear stain using Confocal Imaging Mode.
Optimize the laser power and exposure time for Hoechst nuclear staining.
Use excitation 405, emission 450/50 Bandpass (BP), 500 ms exposure time, and 50% laser power for Hoechst.
Optimize the laser power and exposure time for secondary antibody conjugated to Alexa Fluor (AF) 488.
Use excitation 488, emission 525/50 BP, 500 ms exposure time, and 50% laser power for AF 488.
Optimize the laser power and exposure time for secondary antibody conjugated to AF568.
Use excitation 561, emission 600/50 BP, 500 ms exposure time, and 100% laser power for AF568.
Place the device in the microscope slide device holder with the top chamber facing up.
Set the device in the microscope using a microscope slide holder.
Turn on Live and select the channel for the nuclear stain.
Find the membrane using a low objective, ensuring that the transparent silicon-nitride membrane region is centered.
Switch to the 40x objective, wet the objective, and focus on the membrane region using the nuclear stain as a guide.
Turn on z-stack imaging and set Scan Mode to Start/End.
Set the step size or count using the coarse adjustment knob on the microscope.
Set the scan start to the top of the endothelial cell layer using the nuclear stain as a guide.
Set the scan end at the bottom of the pericyte layer, using the nuclear stain as a guide.
Check all channels to ensure that everything will be captured in the imaging field.
Press Acquire to start imaging.
Repeat on different regions as needed.
Drag the image file into Imaris to open it.
Select Section on the top menu bar to view a 2D image of the x-y plane and corresponding views of the x-z and y-z planes.
Select 3D View on the top menu bar to see a 3D image.
Click on the image and drag it to rotate.
Select Snapshot on the top menu bar to take an image.
Prepare a fluorescent small molecule solution at a concentration of 150 µg/mL.
Prepare an excess volume of the fluorescent small molecule solution for standard solutions.
Replace the medium in the top well with 100 µL of the fluorescent small molecule solution.
Use a hydrophobic pen to draw circles around the sampling ports.
Wait until the hydrophobic ink dries completely before adding the fluorescent dye solution.
Stagger the addition of the fluorescent small molecule solution into the top wells.
Incubate the devices at 37 °C, 5% CO2 for 1 h.
Prepare standard solutions by performing 2-fold serial dilutions from the fluorescent small molecule solution prepared at step 4.1.3.
Pipette 50 μL of each solution into a flat-bottom black 96-well plate in triplicates.
Use blank cell culture medium as the baseline standard solution.
Transfer 200 µL of the excess fluorescent small molecule solution prepared at step 4.1.3 into a tube containing 200 µL of medium.
Mix well and transfer 200 µL of this solution into the next tube containing 200 µL of medium.
Repeat 1:2 dilutions until there are a total of 10 tubes.
Pipette 50 µL of the most concentrated standard solution into column 1 in triplicates (B1, C1, D1).
Pipette 50 µL of the 2nd most concentrated solution into column 2 (B2, C2, D2), and so on.
Pipette 50 µL of blank media in triplicates for the 12th column in the plate (B12, C12, D12).
Remove the fluorescent small molecule solution from the well to stop the process of diffusion.
Place a tip containing 50 µL of medium into the upper port to serve as a reservoir.
Insert the tip with 50 µL into the port, lift the device, and gently eject the tip while holding on to the top for stabilization.
Set down the device.
Add 50 µL of medium into the top well to prevent disruption of the cell monolayer during sampling.
Push a pipetter with an empty pipet tip to its first resistance.
Insert the tip into the sampling port.
Reverse pipet out 50 µL of the solution from the bottom channel.
Transfer directly into the flat-bottom black 96-well plate containing the standard solutions.
Measure the fluorescence intensity in a microplate reader using 428 nm excitation and 536 nm emission wavelengths.
Subtract the averaged fluorescence intensity value of the blank medium from all measured fluorescence intensity values.
Calculate the system permeability Ps using equation (1).
Determine [A]A by plotting a standard curve from the fluorescence intensity outputs and known concentrations of the standard solutions.
Insert fluorescence intensity values of experimental samples into the equation to calculate their concentrations.
